newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF posts higher sales in agriculture unit.
newsitem.headline: BASF posts higher sales in agriculture unit.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG on Wednesday said its crop protection unit had posted a 31 percent rise in sales during the first half of the year driven largely by a large acquisition.
In a statement the group said the unit had posted a 31 percent rise to $1.328 billion. Translated into marks the rise would represent a 47 percent increase to 2.244 billion marks, BASF said.
The main reason for the developments was a smooth integration of the corn herbicides business which BASF acquired from Swiss group Sandoz nearly one year ago.
Sandoz sold its U.S.-Canadian corn herbicides business to BASF for $695 million plus about $83 million in net working capital as a condition for its merger with its rival Ciba-Geigy AG.
BASF said its operating profits rose at an over- proportional rate as compared with the rise in sales, but it declined to give further details.

"What is very important is that this growth was not based solely on one single product or nation but is broad based encompassing all important product areas and regions," said Peter Oakley, head of the unit.
Herbicides posted the strongest gains, rising 47 percent to $805 million or 1.36 billion marks. Fungicides climbed by 15 percent to $387 million or 654 million marks.
North America posted the strongest increase in business with sales rising by 87 percent to $568 million which translates into a 109 percent jump to 959 million marks.
In eastern Europe, Africa and western Asia sales climbed by 27 percent to $56 million which would represent a 44 percent rise to 95 million marks.
Sales in west and central Europe advanced by five percent to $567 million or by 18 percent to 958 million marks.
